name: @kitchensink/ingredient-parser-infra
//: ⛔ NOT AN npm WORKSPACE. Infra installs on its own so `aws-cdk-lib` never enters the root tree.
⚠️ ingredient-parser gains no IMAGE from this — ADR-0025 makes it a Python Lambda with no container. It
moves for the other half of the reason: while its CDK deps sat on the SERVICE they kept aws-cdk-lib in the
root tree for every workspace package, which is exactly what this change removes.
⚠️ Its two packaging integration suites MOVED here from `../tests`. They exercise `lib/packaging.ts` and
`lib/assetContents.ts` — infra code — and reaching them from the service's test directory became a
cross-package relative import the moment this directory stopped being part of that package.
⚠️ `@kitchensink/ingredient-parser` is IMPORTED but not DECLARED: it is an unpublished workspace package,
so declaring it would make `npm install` here resolve it from the registry and 404. Node finds it by
walking up to the repo root. Same trade as every other CDK directory.

scripts.deploy: npm run bundle:lambda --prefix .. && cdk deploy --app 'npx tsx bin/app.ts'
scripts.synth: npm run bundle:lambda --prefix .. && cdk synth --app 'npx tsx bin/app.ts'

localSandbox.skipSynth: its `synth` runs the service's `bundle:lambda` first, which shells out to `python3 -m pip` for ~90 MB of arm64 wheels plus the 1.6 MB CRF model (ADR-0025). A local sandbox must not require a Python toolchain or network to START, and this stack contributes nothing a local run stands up: `awsResources.ts` creates no `AWS::Lambda::Function`, and `localCrfEngine.ts` runs `src/handler.py` directly. Set LOCAL_SANDBOX_SYNTH_ALL=1 to include it.
